articleTitle: Multipath and interference in spread-spectrum tracking systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Spread Spectrum Techniques for Radio Communication Systems
abstract: Multipath tracking errors are analyzed for both coherent and noncoherent delay lock loops with arbitrary early-late spacings, thereby extending the work presented to ION GPS-91, Albuquerque, NM, USA (Sept. 1991: Proceedings p.915-24). The ratios of fading bandwidth, loop bandwidth and data rate are crucial. Maximum absolute multipath pseudorange errors are proportional to early-late spacing, but aggravated by spread-spectrum signal filtering.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Spread Spectrum Techniques for Radio Communication Systems
abstract: This paper proposes the combination of m-ary code shift keying with forward error correction techniques. It has been shown that mCSK could in principle increase capacity of a single CDMA channel several fold, to one third to half the capacity of TDMA. Only Reed-Solomon codes, are considered for this application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Software estimation of CDMA user capacity
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Spread Spectrum Techniques for Radio Communication Systems
abstract: The aim is to determine the potential number of users which a direct-sequence CDMA system could support for a given spreading code, and to show the performance improvement that can be obtained with suitable code selection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Spread Spectrum Techniques for Radio Communication Systems
abstract: The optimum and a suboptimum NEar-FAr Resistant (NEFAR) receiver are presented, with the suboptimum decorrelating detector whose complexity is linear with the number of users. There is strong similarity between the decorrelating detector and adaptive equalization structures used extensively in mobile telephony as a means of combating intersymbol interference. These structures are based on linear adaptive equalization technology and their computational complexity is also linear with the number of users, while their performance is only slightly degraded in comparison with the optimum detector. Nonlinear multiuser equalization techniques are addressed. The validity of the main assumption in this analysis, the correct delay estimation, is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Factors affecting spectral efficiency in a CDMA cellular network
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Spread Spectrum Techniques for Radio Communication Systems
abstract: The authors examine the factors which affect the capacity of a CDMA system in order to arrive at a realistic estimate of the improvement which may be achieved. The evaluation is based on simulations of the reuse interference, voice activity levels and required energy-per-bit/noise-energy ratio. A capacity exceeding twice that of half-rate GSM appears to be possible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of a modified log-likelihood detector for direct sequence spread spectrum
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Spread Spectrum Techniques for Radio Communication Systems
abstract: Computer simulation is used to show that the proposed detector has a significant improvement over the simple log-likelihood detector.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of internal diversity architectures in urban service areas with cellular DS-CDMA systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Spread Spectrum Techniques for Radio Communication Systems
abstract: This paper presents results concerning both the mean signal levels and other statistics of each internal diversity branch of a DS-CDMA receiver for various chipping rates or spreading bandwidths whilst working in an urban environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reduction of the near-far effect in a fast-frequency-hopping receiver
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Spread Spectrum Techniques for Radio Communication Systems
abstract: Given the wide-bandwidth required by a fast frequency-hopping radio system, it is likely there will be occasions when another frequency-hopping user or a conventional narrow-band transmitter will be close to a fast-frequency-hopping (FFH) receiver and vice versa. The abrupt changes in the signal produced by the synthesizer in a FFH receiver, when mixed with the interfering signal, produce interference at the IF. The number of channels affected by this class of interference is calculated. It is shown that the number is reduced dramatically if the receiver's synthesizer output is muted during each frequency change.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of a direct-sequence spread spectrum receiver for a UHF multipath channel
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Spread Spectrum Techniques for Radio Communication Systems
abstract: It is shown that use of the inherent multipath diversity of the received signal an improve the bit error rate performance greatly in the digital RAKE receiver. The key to good performance is in the quality of the channel's impulse response estimation, dependent on tracking filter response. The receiver benefits from relatively low complexity and can track fading at mobile radio channel rates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A spread-spectrum split-signal technique for flexible use of frequency bands
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Spread Spectrum Techniques for Radio Communication Systems
abstract: The paper describes a novel technique for use with direct-sequence spread-spectrum (DS-SS) radio-positioning systems. A high-rate pseudorandom (PN) sequence is sampled to provide a number of lower-rate sequences which are then used to modulate different carriers. These low-rate signals are transmitted to a receiver where they are recombined to recover the original high-rate PN sequence on which conventional range measurements are made. It is shown that the range resolution which can be achieved at a receiver by use of the split-signal format is comparable with what can be achieved by use of a conventional wideband SS signal.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a spread spectrum system for use in impulsive noise
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Spread Spectrum Techniques for Radio Communication Systems
abstract: The authors aim to show that spread spectrum systems have inherent advantages in impulsive noise and that these can be further enhanced by a nonlinear clipping device. The analysis concentrates on matched filter despreading rather than the assumed perfect demodulation. Simulation results and theoretical predictions for a 511-tap matched filter are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The performance of linear modulation through a frequency hopped channel
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Spread Spectrum Techniques for Radio Communication Systems
abstract: This paper considers the implementation of a frequency hopping modem utilising a highly bandwidth efficient linear modulation scheme. The bandwidth of the narrowband message is minimised, and differential operation provides resilience to fading and the nonlinearity of the FH channel. The performance of a single user system has been derived through simulation, with a novel approach for modelling of the FH channel. Instead of simulating a frequency hopper, transmitting through a wideband channel and de-hopping the FH signal at the receiver, the system uses a narrowband 'hopping' channel model, which alters its characteristics to reflect those of the FH propagation environment. To validate this model, measurements have been undertaken into the nature of propagation through the channel. The results are presented in terms of the fading undergone by a hopped signal, and the statistics of that signal at the receiver.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effect of power control error on the capacity of a direct sequence CDMA system for mobile radio
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Spread Spectrum Techniques for Radio Communication Systems
abstract: Errors within the power control process affecting the capacity of the uplink of a DS-CDMA system are considered. They are assumed to result in a composite error which is modelled as being log-normally distributed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
